Eighteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time August 2 2026 This weekend Aug 1st 2nd the Church celebrates the Eighteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time Our Gospel highlights the one miracle that is shared in all four Gospel accounts The Feeding of the Five Thousand Not only is this miracle recounted in each Gospel but both Sts Mark and Matthew record an almost identical second miracle in The Feeding of the Four Thousand which occurs in Gentile territory and is essentially the Gentile sequel to this miracle These accounts The Feeding of the Five Thousand Matthew 1413 21 and The Feeding of the Four Thousand Matthew 1532 38 are of great importance together as they foreshadow the inclusion of both Jew and Gentile in the Church The twelve wicker baskets remaining in the former represent the Twelve Tribes of Israel and the seven in the latter represent wholeness as Christ's abundance will extend beyond Israel to all nations In both accounts Jesus entrusts the food once blessed to His disciples to distribute among the people The role of the disciples here is not incidental It serves a living icon of the Church Christ blesses and multiplies Christ is the bread And still He wills that His gifts be distributed to His people through the hands of His apostles and their successors As then Christ continues to feed us even now by acting through the ministry He entrusts to the apostles Bl Solanus Casey OFM Thank God Ahead of Time This past Thursday July 30th our diocese was one of only five in the world that celebrated the Feast of Bl Solanus Casey Following his beatification in 2017 Bl Solanus Feast Day was added to the local calendars of the dioceses in which he served including our own Bl Solanus arrived at St Felix Friary in nearby Huntington on April 25 1946 He remained there as porter for the Friary for over a decade before returning to Detroit shortly before his death Throughout his life Bl Solanus was sought out by countless souls seeking his advice prayers and at times miraculous healings Even when hospitalized in Detroit in the last days of his life numerous other patients sought him out Bl Solanus exemplified the love of Christ as he gave himself over to God everyday by giving himself to others until there was nothing left to give That love did not end when his earthly life did Those who have gone before us marked with the sign of faith are not separated from us but remain part of the same family of God Just as so many sought Bl Solanus assistance while here on earth we can continue to ask his assistance as he now stands in the Lords presence for all eternity Like all the Saints Bl Solanus only desire is to bring us ever closer to Jesus who alone is the source of every grace and the answer to every prayer Perhaps Bl Solanus greatest lesson is found in the simple phrase he is most known for Thank God ahead of time These words are an act of profound trust Before he saw Gods answer he thanked Him Before he understood Gods plan he praised Him May we ask Bl Solanus to pray that we too might grow in such confidence that whatever lies before us we entrust it to Christ with grateful hearts even before we see how He will answer Time Away in August and Welcoming Fr Theodore As you may recall I am completing a longstanding thesis for my licentiate through Catholic University of America I had previously requested to take leave from the parish to complete this work and have now received permission from the diocese to do so This means that I will be away from the parish next weekend through August 23rd to work with my advisor and complete my thesis regarding parish registration in the United States This leave is only possible because the diocese is assigning Fr Theodore Ekwem to our parish throughout the next three weekends Fr Theodore is a priest of the Diocese of Ekwulobia in southeast Nigeria and assisting in our diocese for the next few months In November he will serve as an observer at our diocesan synod before then
